## Proof

**Claim:** Yes, such a δ > 0 exists.

**Setup.** Let $S = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|x\| = 1\}$ be the unit sphere. Since $n \ge 2$, $S$ is closed and bounded in $\mathbb{R}^n$, hence compact (Heine–Borel). The family $\{U_\alpha\}$ is an open cover of $S$ (open in $\mathbb{R}^n$).

**Constructing a finite subcover with radii.** For each point $p \in S$, there exists some index $\alpha(p)$ with $p \in U_{\alpha(p)}$. Since $U_{\alpha(p)}$ is open in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there is a radius $r_p > 0$ such that the open ball $B(p, r_p) \subset U_{\alpha(p)}$.

The collection $\{B(p, r_p/2) \cap S : p \in S\}$ is an open cover of $S$ in the subspace topology. By compactness of $S$, there exist finitely many points $p_1, \dots, p_k \in S$ such that
$$S \subset \bigcup_{i=1}^{k} B(p_i, r_{p_i}/2).$$

**Choosing δ.** Set
$$\delta = \frac{1}{2}\min_{1 \le i \le k} r_{p_i} > 0.$$

**Verifying the shell is covered.** Take any $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $1 - \delta < \|x\| < 1 + \delta$. Let $p = x / \|x\| \in S$ (note $\|x\| > 1 - \delta > 0$, so this is well-defined). By the finite subcover, there exists $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ with $p \in B(p_i, r_{p_i}/2)$, i.e.,
$$\|p - p_i\| < \frac{r_{p_i}}{2}.$$

Now bound the distance from $x$ to $p_i$:
$$\|x - p_i\| \le \|x - p\| + \|p - p_i\|.$$

Since $p = x/\|x\|$, we have $\|x - p\| = \big|\|x\| - 1\big| < \delta$. Therefore
$$\|x - p_i\| < \delta + \frac{r_{p_i}}{2} \le \frac{r_{p_i}}{2} + \frac{r_{p_i}}{2} = r_{p_i}.$$

Hence $x \in B(p_i, r_{p_i}) \subset U_{\alpha(p_i)}$. Since $x$ was an arbitrary point of the shell $\{x : 1 - \delta < \|x\| < 1 + \delta\}$, we conclude
$$\{x : 1 - \delta < \|x\| < 1 + \delta\} \subset \bigcup_{i=1}^{k} U_{\alpha(p_i)} \subset \bigcup_\alpha U_\alpha.$$

Thus $\{U_\alpha\}$ covers the entire shell. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
